title: Creasvalley CC Clubhouse / LJL Architects
text:
Creasvalley CC Clubhouse / LJL Architects

Even an artificially constructed site can become a landscape as time accumulates. Topography, vegetation, light, and seasonal change establish a distinct order, within which architecture takes its place. The clubhouse is conceived not as an object from which to view its surroundings, but as a mediator through which the site is experienced through terrain, sightlines, and the relationship between inside and outside. The design began by observing this inherent order and exploring how architecture could engage with it.

title: Montana Farm / Estudio Balzano
text:
Montana Farm / Estudio Balzano

Montana Farm is a boutique equestrian breeding and training facility located in Buenos Aires, Argentina, dedicated to the selective breeding and high-level training of show jumping horses. The project was conceived to integrate architecture, landscape, and the specific needs of horses within a contemporary equestrian complex, prioritizing animal welfare, functionality, and spatial quality.

title: Relámpago House  / h3o architects
text:
Relámpago House / h3o architects

The house, with a gable roof, is characterized by the materialization of lightning as a central element that defines and separates the interior spaces. The lightning, when transformed into a wall and luminaire, clearly and immediately structures and shapes the functioning of the different rooms.

title: Ombria Hotel and Apartments Loulé / PROMONTORIO
text:
Ombria Hotel and Apartments Loulé / PROMONTORIO

Quinta da Ombria is a property in the Algarve hinterland with 150 hectares. Surrounded by extensive citrus groves, fig and carob trees, small farms and villages, the dramatic landscape and the rich biodiversity of this mountainous estate comprise a watercourse and a series of archaeological remnants related to farming and its early waterworks. The resort comprises golf course, hotel and clubhouse, in addition to villas and other residential units.

title: Dunhua Tower / Oyler Wu Collaborative
text:
Dunhua Tower / Oyler Wu Collaborative

Rising 17 stories above one of Taipei's principal promenades, Dunhua Tower redefines the residential high-rise typology through a sophisticated interplay of materiality, geometry, and sustainable design. The tower's distinctive L-shaped footprint creates two contrasting facades—one slender and elegantly proportioned, the other broader and more commanding—allowing the building to respond dynamically to its urban context while maximizing natural light and views for residents. Housing 45 residential units, the building achieves an intimate scale that distinguishes it from the typical density of Taipei's housing market.

title: Plaza Salamero: Infrastructure, Landscape, and City / Hector Fernández Elorza
text:
Plaza Salamero: Infrastructure, Landscape, and City / Hector Fernández Elorza

The remodeling of Plaza de Salamero arose from a public competition launched by the Zaragoza City Council to replace the roof slab of the existing underground parking garage beneath the square, following a structural failure detected in 2020. Rather than viewing this circumstance as a limitation, the project turns it into an opportunity to redefine the public space and create a new urban park for the historic center.

title: Learning from Capitalism: How Postmodern Architecture Became the Language of American Business
text:
Learning from Capitalism: How Postmodern Architecture Became the Language of American Business

In 1972, Robert Venturi, Denise Scott Brown, and Steven Izenour published Learning from Las Vegas, challenging architects to reconsider the underappreciated, largely dismissed commercial landscape in the United States. Their storied distinction between the "duck," a building whose form communicates its meaning, and the "decorated shed," an ordinary structure whose identity is conveyed through signs and symbols, questioned a widely accepted modernist assumption that architectural expression should emerge from form and function. By examining billboards, neon lights, casinos, and the commercial strips of Las Vegas, the authors argued that architecture should study the visual languages of American consumer culture.

title: Residential house in Vilnius / Architectural Bureau G.Natkevicius & Partners
text:
Residential house in Vilnius / Architectural Bureau G.Natkevicius & Partners

The project was implemented in an exceptional location in Vilnius – the Aukštagiris Geomorphological Reserve. The protected forest environment and hilly terrain became the main axis of this architectural concept. The landscape dictated the position of the buildings on the plot, allowing for maximum use of natural light, opening up the most spectacular views through the windows, and maintaining a respectful, sustainable relationship with nature.

title: Ikebukuro Living Furniture - Tram Stop / Yosuke SAGOSHI Atelier
text:
Ikebukuro Living Furniture - Tram Stop / Yosuke SAGOSHI Atelier

This broad avenue, extending from Ikebukuro Station toward Marunouchi, was once traversed by Toden trams, with a terminal located right in front of the station. Lines ran from Ikebukuro toward Ueno and Sukiyabashi. One can only imagine the myriad stories that must have unfolded at those stops.

title: Legombang Treehouse / Cave Urban
text:
Legombang Treehouse / Cave Urban

Legombang Treehouse reinterprets traditional Balinese architecture as a contemporary tropical family home, using reclaimed timber, passive design, and a treehouse-like structure woven around the site's existing trees. Designed by Cave Urban co-founder Jed Long for his own family, the house is located in Pantai Lembeng, Ketewel, Bali. As both architect and client, Jed had the opportunity to explore his own approach to tropical family living without the constraints of a conventional client brief.

title: La Joya / Veö estudio
text:
La Joya / Veö estudio

On a plot of land that rises thirteen meters (forty-three feet) from the street, "La Joya" House transforms the challenge of a steep slope into an architectural journey, revealing the landscape of San Agustinillo level by level.
The project emerged from a brief to develop three independent units: two small apartments intended primarily as rentals, and a larger residence for the owners' temporary stays. Instead of concentrating the program into a conventional volume, the steep topography offered an opportunity to fragment it and distribute it across different levels along the hillside. Consequently, each unit finds its own place within the site, maintaining privacy while enjoying a direct relationship with the sea.

title: JCB House / SUITE
text:
JCB House / SUITE

Located in São Paulo, JCB House is a 450-square-meter single-family residence designed by SUITE based on a precise and quiet premise: to create an architecture that presents itself in its most essential form, allowing life to unfold naturally. Developed between 2024 and 2026, the project draws on the interplay of solids and voids to organize integrated spaces that challenge the boundaries between interior and exterior, offering the family a functional, welcoming home open to different ways of living.

title: Herdade da Matinha Country House / Sabrab
text:
Herdade da Matinha Country House / Sabrab

Between the cork oaks and the Vicentina Coast, Herdade da Matinha was born from an abandoned Alentejo estate, whose chimney still bears the date 1917. This rural tourism project, developed by SABRAB Architecture in collaboration with the owner Alfredo Moreira da Silva, starts from a simple principle: to make use of what already existed and add only what was necessary, with the same economy of means that has always characterized rural construction in the Alentejo region.

title: "Camposoto" Health Center / Estudio Suárez Corchete
text:
"Camposoto" Health Center / Estudio Suárez Corchete

The plot is located in a relatively consolidated area of urban expansion, integrated into a block designated for public facilities within a residential environment composed of multi-family apartment buildings and semi-detached single-family homes.

title: Field Shelter in Nara / Studio Armitage
text:
Field Shelter in Nara / Studio Armitage

Field Shelter sits among the allotments and rice fields of Amagatsuji in Nara, Japan. Designed and built by Studio Armitage in collaboration with Space Department, it provides a place for people working on the surrounding plots to sit, rest, and shelter from the weather.

title: Eyes on the Street: Jane Jacobs’ Concept and Contemporary Residential Architecture in Brazil
text:
Eyes on the Street: Jane Jacobs’ Concept and Contemporary Residential Architecture in Brazil

The concept of "eyes on the street" is perhaps the most famous within architectural and urban literature when it comes to urban security. Jane Jacobs uses this expression to refer to people who - consciously or unconsciously - use public spaces or observe them from their homes, generating natural surveillance. A movement that, within our discipline, is encouraged both through quality public spaces and through the powerful relationship between the public and private created through building facades. Advocating for this daily control, Jacobs believes in a way of making architecture and cities that condemns excessive verticalization, reinforced by isolated buildings and single-use ones that deny contact with the street.

title: Family home Eemnes / Kumiki
text:
Family home Eemnes / Kumiki

On the edge of the Zuiderheide nature reserve in Eemnes stands a family home dating from 1971. The original house had a square footprint and measured just fifty square metres. An extension was added in 2002, but this resulted in a fragmented layout. The staircase was hidden away in a corner, the rooms were dark, and the spaces were poorly connected, both visually and in terms of circulation.

title: Colien House / Álvaro Siza Vieira
text:
Colien House / Álvaro Siza Vieira

The slope related to the access street and the willingness to act just on the essentials, regarding the topography and site vegetation, guided the program organization of Colien House into a compact volume that staged descends the terrain slope.

title: Estúdio Semibreve / Estúdio Clara Nahas
text:
Estúdio Semibreve / Estúdio Clara Nahas

No Estúdio Semibreve, a materialização da narrativa exigiu um exercício rigoroso de zoneamento e uma subversão proposital da lógica habitacional. Em uma área de 55 metros quadrados, o Estúdio Clara Nahas estabelece uma planta de fluxo invertido, onde a hierarquia convencional entre o público e o privado é reordenada para priorizar o recolhimento. Diferente da recepção imediata por áreas sociais, a entrada acontece pela zona íntima. O visitante da mostra é convidado a percorrer o dormitório e o ambiente de estudo antes de alcançar a amplitude da convivência. Esta decisão projetual atua como um filtro sensorial: atravessar a intimidade torna-se um rito de passagem necessário para se conectar com a alma da casa, sugerindo que o despojamento pessoal deve preceder o encontro com o outro.

title: Basque Museum Bilbao / VAILLO + ARCHITECTS
text:
Basque Museum Bilbao / VAILLO + ARCHITECTS

The project is the outcome of a competition for the comprehensive architectural and museographic renovation and rehabilitation of the Euskal Museoa Bilbao—the Ethnographic Museum of Basque Culture. The complex of buildings that makes up the current museum is located on a city block in Bilbao's historic center; its origins date back to the 17th century with the founding of the first Society of Jesus (Jesuit) college in Bilbao in 1600.

title: Veja São Paulo Store / Roberto Somlo Arquitetura
text:
Veja São Paulo Store / Roberto Somlo Arquitetura

The project transforms an existing building on Oscar Freire Street, in the Jardim Paulista neighborhood, to house the first VEJA store in Brazil. The store is a radical encounter between exposed history and São Paulo modernism.

title: CitySquash / Gluck+
text:
CitySquash / Gluck+

CitySquash is a not-for-profit after-school enrichment program serving youth in the Bronx and Brooklyn through an integrated model of athletics, academics and mentorship. As the organization expanded beyond its existing scattered facilities serving more than 225 students annually, a new center was designed within the neighborhood it already serves, bringing these services together into a cohesive whole.

title: Success Academy Bronx K–12 Campus / SOM
text:
Success Academy Bronx K–12 Campus / SOM

Success Academy (SA)—one of the nation's largest and highest-performing public charter networks—educates 22,000 students, primarily from low-income backgrounds, across 60 New York City schools. Founded on the belief that all children can excel when given access to exceptional teaching and learning environments, SA is nationally recognized for its rigorous academics, robust arts and athletics programming, and deep focus on college preparedness. For its first ground-up building, the network charged SOM with creating a 310,000-square-foot K–12 "school of the future," with every aspect of the architecture supporting and reflecting SA's carefully crafted and boldly reinvented schooling practice.

title: Lele Hotel / The Lab Evn
text:
Lele Hotel / The Lab Evn

Located in Vayots Dzor, Lele Hotel is conceived as a direct response to the character and topography of its mountainous surroundings. Rather than imposing a separate architectural object on the landscape, the design seeks continuity with the terrain through its materiality, proportions, and relationship to the existing slope.
